summary:
The name of the bill is the National Service Corps Bill, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to amend and consolidate the legal provisions regarding conducting training of the National Service Corps to prepare patriotic, public-serving, moral, and disciplined human resources by instilling feelings of national unity and respect and pride towards national values among students studying in schools, and to deploy them as volunteers in service of the nation based on national necessity (Preamble, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Under the federal government, the Government of Nepal, Council of Ministers shall approve the organizational structure and posts of the Service Corps on the recommendation of the Ministry (Section 4, Subsection 1). If additional human resources are required, the Government of Nepal may depute human resources from the Nepali Army, civil service of the Government of Nepal, and other services on deputation (Section 4, Subsection 3). The Government of Nepal may deploy students trained under this Act and persons who received training under Section 18 Subsection (1) as volunteers in service of the nation (Section 18, Subsection 3, Page 6). Provisions regarding providing training based on national necessity and deploying as volunteers in service of the nation shall be as determined by the Government of Nepal, Council of Ministers (Section 18, Subsection 4, Page 6). The Service Corps may request necessary assistance from the Government of Nepal, Provincial Government, or Local Level or bodies under them for the implementation of this Act (Section 22, Subsection 1, Page 6). If assistance is requested, the concerned body must provide the necessary assistance (Section 22, Subsection 2, Page 6). When selecting schools, the local body of the Nepali Army must coordinate with the concerned district education office and the local level (Section 14, Subsection 4).

Schools interested in participating in the training must submit an application to the Service Corps office in the format specified by the Committee (Section 14, Subsection 2). Prior to participating in the training, the guardian or protector of the concerned student and the school must submit an agreement in the format specified by the Committee (Section 15, Subsection 5, Page 5). Students selected for training must take an oath in the format specified by the Committee before training begins (Section 15, Subsection 6, Page 5). Every year, the Service Corps must submit a progress report of the work performed by it to the Ministry through the Nepali Army within three months from the date of completion of the financial year (Section 26, Subsection 1, Page 6). The Ministry must publish the progress report submitted accordingly (Section 26, Subsection 2, Page 6).

The training provided to students shall be of two levels, namely Junior Division level and Senior Division level (Section 15, Subsection 1, Page 5). Students studying in classes eight to ten in school shall be eligible to participate in Junior Division level training (Section 15, Subsection 2, Page 5). Students studying in classes eleven and twelve in school shall be eligible to participate in Senior Division level training (Section 15, Subsection 3, Page 5). When selecting for Junior Division training, students who have completed 13 years of age up to not exceeding 18 years, and when selecting for Senior Division training, students who have completed 16 years of age up to not exceeding 21 years must be selected (Section 15, Subsection 4, Page 5). The Academy shall impart training to cadets in at least two stages (Section 16, Subsection 1, Page 5). Training shall be imparted in the first stage at the school where the student studies and in the second stage at the Academy (Section 16, Subsection 2, Page 5). The duration and other methods of conducting training shall be as determined by the Committee (Section 16, Subsection 3, Page 5). Upon completion of training, cadets shall be awarded a certificate (Section 16, Subsection 4, Page 5).

This bill establishes the National Service Corps (called National Cadet Corps in English) to impart necessary training to students studying in schools to prepare patriotic, public-serving, moral, and disciplined human resources (Section 3, Subsection 1, Subsection 3, Page 1). Instilling feelings of national unity and respect and pride towards national values among students shall be its main objective (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 1). Its head office shall be located in the Kathmandu Valley, and it may establish offices in other places of the country as needed (Section 3, Subsection 4, Subsection 5, Page 1, Page 2). To decide on policy matters regarding the operation of the Service Corps and to give necessary directions to the Academy on other matters, there shall be a Director Committee chaired by the Minister of Defence, with the Chief of Army Staff, Secretary of the Ministry of Defence, Secretary of the Ministry of Education and Sports, Master General of Ordnance of the Nepali Army, and the Director General of the Service Corps as member-secretary (Section 6, Page 2). The functions, duties, and powers of the Committee include making policy decisions, approving annual programs, work plans, curriculum, and training methods, and determining criteria (Section 8). To work as the administrative chief of the Service Corps, the Government of Nepal, Council of Ministers shall appoint a Director General from among retired Major Generals for a tenure of 2 years on the recommendation of the Chief of Army Staff (Section 9, Subsection 1, Subsection 2, Page 3). The budget required for the Service Corps shall be managed from within the annual budget ceiling received by the Ministry (Section 19, Page 6).

This Act repeals the National Service Corps Act, 2027 (Section 29, Subsection 1, Page 7). Actions done or taken under the National Service Corps Act, 2027 shal
